description.narrative: The objectives of the Modernizing Higher Education Project for Uzbekistan are to strengthen the Recipient's higher education system managerial capacity, and to improve both the labor market relevance and the learning environment of selected higher education institutions. There are four components to the project, the first component being Strengthening Higher Education Management. The project will support enhancement of the managerial capacity of the higher education system in Uzbekistan by: (a) strengthening the capacity of the MHSSE to manage the sector, (b) supporting the STC to develop and implement the system of external quality assurance, and (c) supporting the HEIs to strengthen their systems of internal quality assurance. The second component is the improving the learning environment in HEIs. The project will support the government in improving laboratories and research systems, to help better prepare higher education graduates to contribute to scientific progress in an effort to increase economic growth. The third component is the improving the relevance of higher education. Finally, the fourth component is the project management, monitoring and evaluation. The component will support incremental operating costs for the project, including a core team of consultants to coordinate the project, ensure fiduciary compliance, and monitor it. The project will also finance technical experts to support implementation, as needed, and studies and evaluations.

The project development objectives are to strengthen the Recipient's higher education system managerial capacity, and to improve both the labor market relevance and the learning environment of selected higher education institutions.

condition.narrative: Finance Agreement :Instituional arrangements | Description :Not later than [ninety (90) days after the effectiveness of thisAgreement] MHSSE shall acquire and install a fully functional automated accounting information system for keeping the Projectrecords and generation of the Project Financial Statements. | Due Date :02-Jan-2017

Finance Agreement :Institutional Arrangements | Description :Not later than [ninety (90) days after the effectiveness of thisAgreement] , the Recipient shall establish, and thereafter maintain, throughout the implementation of the Project, an ExpertAdvisory Panel, consisting of four widely recognized higher education specialists, with at least two of them not being nationals ofthe Recipient, with terms of reference satisfactory to the Association. | Due Date :02-Jan-2017

Finance Agreement :Project Management Team (PMT) | Description: At all times during Project implementation, the Recipient shallensure that the Project Management Team is maintained with adequate funds, suitably qualified staff in sufficient numbers,facilities, services and other resources, including an adequate financial management system, all satisfactory to the Association. |Frequency :Yearly

Finance Agreement :Third Party Monitoring of project (TPM) and Feedback Mechanism (FBM) | Description :The Recipient: (a) shall andshall cause respective local authorities to fully collaborate with the TPM Consultant in developing an effective grievance redressmechanism in connection with the Project activities, as set forth in the TPM Consultant's terms of reference; | Frequency :Yearly

Finance Agreement :Third Party Monitoring of project (TPM) and Feedback Mechanism (FBM) | Description :The Recipient: (b) shallreview biannual reports of the TPM Consultant on grievances received, redress mechanism and any feedback provided;The Recipient:(c) shall promptly implement or cause relevant local authorities to implement the recommendations provided in said reports. |Frequency :Yearly

Finance Agreement: Third Party Monitoring of project (TPM) and Feedback Mechanism (FBM) | Description :The Recipient shall carryout the Project in accordance with this Agreement, appropriate social standards and practices and any applicable laws andregulations on child and forced labor. | Frequency :Yearly

Finance Agreement: Third Party Monitoring of project (TPM) and Feedback Mechanism (FBM) | Description :The Recipient shall take allnecessary actions, and ensure necessary actions are taken, enable the TPM Consultant to perform monitoring activities in accordancewith the applicable TOR, including, but not limited to allowing and facilitating for the TPM Consultant to visit sites where theProject is being carried out, collect relevant data and communicate with Project stakeholder and participants. | Frequency :Yearly

Finance Agreement: Third Party Monitoring of project (TPM) and Feedback Mechanism (FBM) | Description :The Recipient shall: (a)review and discuss with the Bank monitoring reports prepared by the TPM Consultant; and (b) promptly take any actions, as may berequested by the Bank upon its review of said reports, with respect to compliance with the undertakings relating to child and/orforced labor as set forth in this Agreement and the Project Operations Manual. | Frequency :Yearly

title.narrative: Percentage of project-supported HEIs that incorporate citizen engagement into grant proposals under the AIF

comment.narrative:
<p>End target was surpassed. Percentage of project-supported HEIs that incorporate citizen engagement into
grant proposals und er the AIF identified as 100 percent. The Ministry monitors all grants on a quarterly
basis.</p>

title.narrative: Number of basic teaching laboratories established and incorporated in academic programs

comment.narrative: <p>End target is achieved. To date, all 112 basic teaching laboratories have been incorporated in the academic process.</p>

title.narrative: Number of partnerships established under the AIF

comment.narrative:
<p>End target was surpassed. 194 partnerships has been established under the AIF, including 65 international
partnerships. The  reason why this indicator has succeeded is the design of an effective call of proposal
and application process, which aims to  encourage partnerships for grant applications.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of eligible HEIs benefitting from grants of the Competitive Academic Innovation Fund

comment.narrative: <p>End target was surpassed. At the moment percentage of eligible HEIs benefiting from grants of the competitive AIF identified as 41 percent. The project will continue supporting the implementation of these grants and will continue monitoring them.</p>

title.narrative: Number of advanced scientific research laboratories established and incorporated in research programs

comment.narrative: <p>For this indicator end target is achieved. To date, all 7 advanced scientific research laboratories have been incorporated in the academic process.</p>

title.narrative: Number of Staff from State Inspection for Supervision of Quality in Education (SISQE) and experts trained in higher education quality-assurance-related topics

comment.narrative: <p>End target was surpassed. The Ministry and State Inspection for Supervision of Quality in Education highlighted the importance of strengthening the capacity of the institutions for the self-assessment process, and that is the main reason why the target for training staff and experts has been exceeded by so much.</p>
<p>End target was achieved. This number is based on HEMIS beneficiary who obtained diplomas and contracts through HEMIS, AIF b eneficiary and users of teaching laboratories.</p>
<p>End target was achieved. Female participation in higher education is 46.5 percent, according to HEMIS.</p>
<p>End target was achieved. HEMIS operational and implemented in all public universities.</p>

actual.value: HEMIS operational and implemented in all public universities

comment.narrative: <p>End target is achieved. National e-library is developed. Currently, unilibrary consist of more than 125 thousand books, mor e than 7 thousand articles, more than 9 thousand dissertations</p>

title.narrative: Assessment of options to increase female enrolment

comment.narrative: <p>Following the survey, a dissemination workshop was conducted and the report is now available on the MHSSE official web-site . Selection of AIF grants already completed in December 2018.</p>

actual.value: Report on Options to Increase Female Enrolment used to inform selection criteria of grants under AIF.

title.narrative: Percentage of universities that complete institutional self-assessment through Quality Enhancement Cells

comment.narrative: <p>For this indicator end target was achieved and exceeded. To date, out of 70 public HEIs 40 HEIs have completed institutiona l self-assessment through QECs, reaching 57%</p>

title.narrative: Number of modernized learning and research laboratories established and incorporated in revised academic programs

comment.narrative: <p>Exceeded end target. To date, 112 basic teaching laboratories (100%) and 7 advanced research-scientific laboratories have been installed and incorporated in the academic process. </p>

title.narrative: Students benefiting from direct interventions to enhance learning

comment.narrative: <p>This number is based on Elsevier monthly usage report, AIF beneficiaries, and users of distance learning platforms.</p>

title.narrative: Increase in the index of labor market relevance of higher education perceived by students, civil society, and firms

baseline.value: No existing baseline at the beginning of the project. The baseline was established and the index current value is calculated at 58.48%. First Survey

comment.narrative: <p>For this indicator end target was achieved. Based on the final results of the survey relevance of HE is accounted for 78%.</p>
